title: PaperCue: Speaker-Side Cues for Explaining Research Face to Face
abstract: PaperCue helps researchers explain their papers in face-to-face conversations by maintaining an evolving audience model and giving the presenter very short private cues instead of complete answers.
key_contributions: An evolving, evidence-backed audience model that separates profile priors from conversational evidence.
A cue generator that produces short presenter cues grounded in structured paper units.
forbidden_claims: PaperCue reads answers aloud for the presenter
PaperCue has been validated in a user study

units.title: Local processing and data storage
units.content: PaperCue processes conversation data locally and does not upload raw audio. Typed turns and the derived audience model are stored in a local SQLite database that the researcher can export or delete.
units.short_explanation: All processing stays on the presenter's computer; nothing is uploaded.

units.title: Evolving audience model
units.content: The audience model stores explicit beliefs about familiarity, interests, goals, concerns and preferred explanation level. Each belief keeps its confidence, supporting evidence, source turn, and update reason.
units.short_explanation: Beliefs about the listener are updated from conversational evidence.

units.title: Cues, not answers
units.content: PaperCue never writes answers for the presenter. It provides two-to-seven word cues such as 'start with practical use' so the presenter stays in control of the conversation.
units.short_explanation: The system gives short cues; the presenter still does the explaining.

units.title: Poster sessions and lab visits
units.content: Typical uses are poster sessions, lab visits and hallway conversations where a researcher explains the same paper to many listeners with different backgrounds.
units.short_explanation: Useful when one paper is explained to many different listeners.

units.title: Wearable sensing connection
units.content: Cues are designed to be delivered privately through an earbud, which connects PaperCue to wearable sensing and wearable interaction research.
units.short_explanation: Earbud delivery links the work to wearable sensing.

units.title: Explaining the language model simply
units.content: Instead of saying 'a local language model classifies dialogue acts', the presenter can say the system notices whether the listener is asking, doubting, or agreeing.
units.short_explanation: Replace model jargon with what the system notices.

units.title: Latency of local models
units.content: Running the language model locally adds latency, so cues may arrive after the moment has passed. The current prototype uses typed input instead of live speech.
units.short_explanation: Local inference is slow and live speech is not yet supported.
